hook: Ilya Sutskever was born in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, and moved with his family first to Israel and then to Canada, where he studied computer science at the University of Toronto under Geoffrey Hinton. In 2012 he co-authored the AlexNet paper with Alex Krizhevsky and Hinton, a deep convolutional network that sharply cut ImageNet classification error rates and helped launch the modern deep learning era. He followed this in 2014 with Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks, showing that a general encoder-decoder architecture could handle tasks like machine translation. In December 2015 he co-founded OpenAI, serving first as Research Director and later as Chief Scientist while the lab built its GPT model series. He left OpenAI in 2024 and co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy, a company dedicated to a single goal, building safe superintelligence, and became its CEO in mid-2025 after Gross departed.

standing.watch: What is unresolved is mostly on the OpenAI side of the record. The site lists USA Today Co., Inc. v. OpenAI Foundation, TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, and GRANT v. OPENAI INC, all filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. Buist v. Anthropic, PBC is also filed with no development recorded. For Sutskever himself, the records show no pending case and no planned listing, only his mid-2025 move to CEO of Safe Superintelligence Inc after Gross departed. Where the records are thin, they say less, and here they say only that the OpenAI matters remain open.
standing.record: The site's records add up to a technical career that moved from academic deep learning into lab leadership and then into a new venture. He studied computer science at the University of Toronto under Geoffrey Hinton, co-authored AlexNet in 2012, and followed with Sequence to Sequence Learning in 2014. He co-founded OpenAI in December 2015 and left in 2024 to co-found Safe Superintelligence Inc with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy. The lawsuits on the site are filed against OpenAI entities and, in one instance, Anthropic, with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. The pattern is a researcher whose name is tied to foundational papers and to OpenAI's founding, while the legal records attach to the companies rather than to him.
standing.standing: Ilya Sutskever stands as co-founder and CEO of Safe Superintelligence Inc, a company dedicated to a single goal of building safe superintelligence, a role he took in mid-2025 after co-founder Daniel Gross departed. Before that he co-founded OpenAI in December 2015 and served as Research Director and later Chief Scientist while the lab built its GPT model series, leaving in 2024. His standing rests on foundational technical work, including the 2012 AlexNet paper with Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton and the 2014 Sequence to Sequence Learning paper. The records show he now controls a company with one stated purpose rather than a broad product line. The site lists OpenAI as a company he founded, and the lawsuits it holds name OpenAI entities, not him personally.

achievements.title: AlexNet, 2012
achievements.impact: Co-created with Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton, this deep convolutional network dramatically cut ImageNet classification error rates and helped trigger renewed interest in deep neural networks.

achievements.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks, 2014
achievements.impact: Showed that a general-purpose encoder-decoder LSTM architecture could perform machine translation, influencing later neural translation and language systems.

achievements.title: Co-founder, OpenAI, 2015
achievements.impact: Helped set OpenAI's early research agenda as Research Director, and later as Chief Scientist, during development of the GPT series of models.

achievements.title: Co-founder, Safe Superintelligence Inc, 2024
achievements.impact: Built a research lab dedicated to a single product, safe superintelligence, without near-term commercial offerings.
